No matter what anyone says I cannot emphasise this enough: The correct way to drink Scotch is the way that you enjoy it.

Neat keeps the aroma very concentrated and the alcohol has the expected burn to it. Adding ice chills the drink as well as diluting it, meaning that you detect far less of the aroma. This can make it much easier to drink (when you start) although you definitely lose some nuance. Adding a little water avoids this and, contrary to what many say, water opens up whisky and can present entirely new aromas and flavours. Smell before and after adding anything to the whisky and see how it changes - that's the first and easiest step towards appreciation.

Bourbon is easier to start with as it tends to express sweeter notes like caramel and vanilla. Four Roses and Elijah Craig are decent options.

With Scotch, there are two key differentiators when you're new: age and barrel. Age is self-explanatory: older whisky tends to develop smoother, more nuanced flavours but they cost more (and due to diminishing older stock that can't meet demand, many distilleries are putting out No Age Statement whisky instead). Unlike bourbon which is aged in new oak barrels, Scotch is aged by using barrels previously used to aged other drinks, including bourbon, sherry and port. As it ages, it soaks up this character as well as the wood itself. Unless you already know that you're a particular fan of smoky or peaty drinks, I'd recommend starting with sherried whisky, as it tends to be much more mellow - Dalmore, Macallan or Glenfarclas are good examples.

Source: member of the Scotch Malt Whisky Society

If you really just don't like the taste at first, you should acclimate yourself to it first. Start experimenting with mixed drinks and find something you like. Bourbon and Coke, Kentucky Sunrise (1 Bourbon + 2 Orange Juice + .5 Grenadine [or 2-3 dashes of bitters]), etc. From that point, either increase that drink in strength as time progresses or move to a generally stronger drink like an old fashioned (2 bourbon + 1-2 muddled orange slices, 1 simple syrup, 1 ice cube, and a maraschino cherry). When you can enjoy the stronger drink, try sipping 2 shots + 2-4 drops of water in a lowball glass.

For best results, use quality bourbon: Pappy van Winkle if you want the good stuff, followed by the other Old Rip van Winkle products, Woodford Reserve, Maker's Mark, Wild Turkey, Buffalo Trace, etc. Most distilleries sell varying qualities and ages, so pay attention to what you're getting.

Even then, they threw the upper on a new lower and it still fired.

So long as I keep the bolt carrier group wet with oil, I'm not worried. The AR-15 family is built to some pretty specific tolerances, and what that winds up meaning is that it tends to keep a lot of the nasty business out of where it ought to not be in the first place. It's come along way since its vietnam debut.
